Cyprus-People's Republic of China Double Taxation Agreement (in force)
Cyprus-United Kingdom Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: The Prevention and Suppression of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Law, L. 188(I)/2007, as amended, together with the Companies Law, Cap. 113, as amended by the Companies (Amendment) Law No. 67(I)/2021 which establishes the Central Register of Beneficial Owners in Cyprus; EU Anti-Money Laundering Directives (4AMLD/5AMLD) are directly implemented.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national authority in the country of origin (e.g., police or passport issuing ministry)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Evidence of residential address (recent utility bill or bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed bank in the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good conduct / police clearance for each director and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent police or criminal records authority in the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter for each director and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent or primary bank in the banked country

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory customer due diligence under L. 188(I)/2007; mandatory PEP screening and enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons; mandatory screening against the Cyprus consolidated sanctions list, the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, EU Council Regulations, and the OFAC SDN list where USD transactions are contemplated; ongoing transaction monitoring and suspicious transaction reporting to the Cyprus Unit for Combating Money Laundering (FIU).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRCOR) – online name reservation via the Cyprus Companies Registry electronic portal (https://portal.drcor.mcit.gov.cy)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be registered in Greek or English or both; where a Greek name is used, a Latin-character transliteration is mandatory for electronic registry indexing; names must not be identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names; abbreviations permitted in accordance with DRCOR guidelines.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: An administrative appeal must be filed in writing with DRCOR within 14 days of the rejection notice, setting out the legal grounds and any proposed amendments; if DRCOR upholds the refusal, recourse may be initiated under Article 146 of the Constitution before the Administrative Court within 75 days of the decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for statutory registration provided a registered office address in Cyprus is maintained and a licensed corporate service provider is appointed as registered agent; however, for tax residence and economic substance the company must demonstrate central management and control in Cyprus, and a mere virtual office without any physical substance may be challenged by the Cyprus Tax Department or by banks for operational purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (less than 10% annual probability) for a non-regulated standard-risk design-as-a-service company; risk may rise to 25-50% if the company seeks CySEC licensing, obtains payment institution status, or exhibits unusual AML/CFT transaction patterns.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law (Cap. 113), Sections 4, 5, 7, 8, 10, 11, 51, and 73 (Republic of Cyprus)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DROC), Nicosia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form HE1 – Application for Registration of a Private Company together with Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; a private limited company may lawfully commence operations with an issued capital of €1. There is no escrow account or deposit requirement under Cyprus law for non-regulated industries.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the company adopts its Memorandum and Articles of Association as filed, and that the founding subscriber irrevocably subscribes for one hundred (100) ordinary shares at €1 par value each, fully paid, allocated in accordance with the submitted statement of capital. RESOLVED that the registered office of the company is fixed at the address appearing in the official registers, within the Republic of Cyprus, and that any change of address shall be notified to the Registrar without delay. RESOLVED that the persons named in the consent forms are appointed as the first directors and the company secretary, each having accepted office, and are collectively authorised to open bank accounts, execute commercial contracts, engage professional advisors, and complete all statutory filings and payments required for incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Registered Office Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DROC), Nicosia — online through the Ariadni portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form HE13 for company name reservation through the Ariadni online system or physically at DROC. The proposed name must end with 'Limited' or 'Ltd' and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing Cyprus name or protected EU trademark. Concurrently verify that the intended registered office address in Cyprus is available for service of process and that the landlord or sublessor consents to use of the premises for corporate registrations.
required_dossiers: Form HE13 – Name Reservation Request
Proposed company name in Latin characters
Identification details of the founding shareholder (certified passport copy)
Consent of the registered office property owner or lease agreement extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or placed on objection, file a new HE13 with three alternative names within 14 days. If a third-party objection is raised, submit a written response and, if the objection is upheld, choose a different name or request a formal review by DROC within the statutory period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DROC / Certifying Lawyer licensed in Cyprus
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association (M&A) to comply with the First and Second Schedules of the Companies Law (Cap. 113) as applicable to a private limited company. The M&A must be signed by the founding subscriber, witnessed, and the subscriber's shareholding recorded. The Articles must include directors' powers, share transfer restrictions, and statutory meeting provisions. If any director or secretary is non-resident, ensure their consents to act are signed and notarised where required.
required_dossiers: Memorandum of Association
Articles of Association
Form HE31 – Consent to Act of Director (if applicable)
Form HE32 – Consent to Act of Secretary (if applicable)
Identification documents for each director, secretary, and shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry or the certifying counsel identifies a legal deficiency in the M&A, revise the inconsistent clauses and re-certify. Re-submit the corrected version to DROC with a cover letter explaining the amendment; the review clock restarts from the date of complete resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission of Incorporation Application and Fee Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form HE1 (Application for Incorporation) through the Ariadni electronic system, attaching the executed M&A, consents of directors and secretary, and the name reservation receipt. Pay the official filing fee (currently approximately €156) and any applicable stamp duty on share capital (maximum €20). Verify that all signatures are in PDF format and that certified translations of foreign-language documents, if any, are attached.
required_dossiers: Form HE1 – Application for Registration of a Private Company
Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association (signed PDF)
Name reservation certificate (HE13 approval)
Certified copies of passport of all subscribers and officers
Evidence of registered office address (lease or ownership deed)
Receipt of payment of incorporation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DROC issues a query (HE2 letter), respond within the specified time frame (usually 15 days) with the requested clarifications or corrected documents. If the application is rejected, correct the stated defects and resubmit within 30 days to retain priority; otherwise file a new application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful examination, DROC registers the company and issues the Certificate of Incorporation. The certificate assigns the company registration number (HE or HE77 series). The company legally exists as a separate legal personality from the moment of issuance. Download the certified electronic certificate from Ariadni or collect the physical copy from the Registry.
required_dossiers: Approved incorporation application (internal DROC record)
Certificate of Incorporation (issued by DROC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is not issued within the indicative SLA, contact DROC through the Ariadni portal or in person to request expeditious release. In case of errors in the certificate (e.g., incorrect name or number), submit a written correction request along with the original certificate and supporting incorporation documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office Setup, Statutory Registers, and Beneficial Ownership Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DROC / Company Secretary / Cyprus Tax Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, physically establish the registered office in Cyprus and ensure that the address is effective for service of legal processes. Prepare and maintain statutory registers of members, directors, secretaries, and charges. File the Beneficial Ownership (BO) declaration with DROC within 30 days of incorporation if the company falls under the Beneficial Ownership Register rules. If the company is engaged in taxable activities, apply for a Tax Identification Code (TIC) from the Cyprus Tax Department at this stage, as it is not part of the incorporation filing but is needed for banking and onboarding.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Registered office consent letter from landlord
Form HE for Director/Secretary particulars (if not already filed)
Beneficial ownership declaration (BO form)
Tax registration form (TD 2001, if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BO declaration is queried for inconsistencies, provide corrected ownership details and supporting chain-of-title documents within 30 days. If the registered office is found to be non-compliant without a physical presence, arrange a substitute compliant address and file a change of registered office notice (Form HE45) promptly.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – ISIC 7410 (Product Interface Design and Digital Design Subscription Agency) is a non-industrial, non-manufacturing, and non-extractive activity under Cyprus law and does not require an industrial establishment license.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required. The company may operate solely on the strength of its Certificate of Incorporation, Tax Registration, and any professional intellectual-property consents. If physical office space is leased, standard municipal business registration may apply but is not an industrial permit.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Cyprus Department of Environment, Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 5 – Exempt / Not subject to Environmental Impact Assessment under Annex III of the EIA Act. Office-based professional services with no industrial effluent, no combustion plant, and no waste-generation threshold trigger no EIA screening.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No applicable wastewater or VOC discharge thresholds for pure desk-based design activities. General municipal waste handling must comply with the Cyprus Waste Management Law (L. 185(I)/2011) and any building-level waste management plan. If the office building uses air conditioning and lighting, relevant energy-efficiency and electrical safety standards (EN/IEC) apply, but no emissions limits specific to design services apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The company must comply with the Cyprus Fire Safety Regulations (Fire Protection and Extinguishing Equipment Law, L. 118(I)/2018) for its office premises, including fire extinguisher certification, emergency exits, and fire safety signage. The Department of Labour Inspection (Ministry of Labour, Welfare and Social Insurance) may carry out an occupational health and safety inspection under the Safety and Health at Work Law (L. 89(I)/1996). For a standard leased office, a civil defence clearance is not independently required, but the building occupancy certificate and fire safety certificate must be verified and maintained. If the company later opens a physical showroom or prototyping lab, separate municipal building and fire-safety permits will be triggered.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Tax Department, Ministry of Finance, Republic of Cyprus; official e-portal: https://taxportal.cy
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity that is not otherwise established in Cyprus must apply through the Tax Portal before making taxable supplies. The electronic procedure requires verified company information (certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, registered address), beneficial-owner identification declarations, evidence of business activity, and the appointment of a Cyprus tax representative where required. A taxpayer identification number (TIN, identical to the VAT number) is issued upon approval. No minimum capital is required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or classification election exists under Cyprus law. A private limited company is per se a separate taxable person; residence is a factual management-and-control test. Cyprus applies ATAD 2 hybrid mismatch rules and controlled-foreign-company provisions that override mismatches; no statutory pass-through election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Cyprus VAT Law No. 94(I)/2000 (EU-aligned)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 15,600 annual taxable turnover for established taxable persons; EUR 10,000 for intra-Community distance sales; non-established foreign suppliers have no threshold and must register before making taxable supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API mandate, or digital stamping regime is in force. Mandatory B2G e-invoicing applies for Cypriot public-sector purchases through the national Ariadne platform; B2B e-invoicing continues under mutual consent with PDF/XML retention rules.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: zero-rating applies where goods are exported outside the European Union in accordance with the Cyprus VAT Law; the supplier must ship the goods pursuant to an export contract and hold contemporaneous evidence. Services (including UI/UX design subscriptions): zero-rating is applicable to certain export-related services; other digital design services supplied to clients outside Cyprus are normally outside the territorial scope of Cyprus VAT under the place-of-supply rules where the recipient is a taxable person established in a third country, or if the services are treated as legal/technical/intellectual equivalent categories; all export invoices must display the zero-rating reason code and retain evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (formal SAD export declaration)
Bill of Lading (or equivalent transport documentation: AWB/CMR)
Inward Remittance Certificate (or bank payment evidence)
Commercial invoice and export packing list
Evidence of buyer's non-EU taxable status (VAT/GST number or legal proof)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Cyprus Tax Department verifies zero-rated export claims before crediting refunds. Missing or unreliable documentation triggers reversal of the zero-rating and assessment to VAT at 19%, plus interest and administrative penalties; the supplier bears the burden of proof. Deliberate false declarations expose the company and its officers to criminal liability, substantial fines, and imprisonment, and the Tax Department may claw back refunds plus penalties and extend the statutory limitation period in cases of fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Cyprus (Κεντρική Τράπεζα της Κύπρου)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Cyprus is a Member State of the European Union and part of the Eurozone. Both current and capital account transactions are fully liberalised; no separate foreign-exchange control regime is maintained. Profit remittances, dividends, and loan repayments to non-residents may be executed without exchange-control approval, subject only to anti-money laundering verification and EU/UN sanctions screening.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. The Republic of Cyprus imposes no statutory obligation to repatriate, surrender, or convert export proceeds. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency or converted to euro at commercial banks, subject to customer due diligence measures.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Cyprus Public Company Ltd
Bank of Cyprus Public Company Ltd

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility. Cyprus-recognised Electronic Money Institutions and payment institutions, including EU-passported fintechs such as Wise and Stripe Treasury-affiliated partners, can operate alongside commercial banks. For the design-subscription business model, fintech EMI rails are viable for collections and disbursements; however, they typically do not provide credit facilities or escrow services, and high-volume euro clearing should retain at least one domestic correspondent bank relationship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of directors is not statutorily mandated for a Cypriot private limited company. Cypriot banks generally permit remote onboarding via video-conference KYC when the corporate structure is transparent and beneficial owners are identifiable. Some tier-1 banks may nonetheless require an in-person attend at a branch or at a Cyprus-based professional services firm for signing wet-ink resolutions or verifying original identification documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident director or shareholder in a jurisdiction with FATF/CRS high-risk classification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport of all individuals; proof of address (utility bill or bank statement under 6 months); professional reference from a reputable international bank; share registry and register of beneficial owners excerpt; tax residence certificate; updated due diligence questionnaire evidencing source of wealth and source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex multi-tier ownership or trust/nominee participation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion from a licensed Cyprus lawyer on the chain of ownership; organisational chart; trust instrument or nominee declaration; proof of economic substance in Cyprus (lease, employment records, accounting agent contract) to rebut shell-company classification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk revenue stream flagged by bank due to digital subscription model with recurring cross-border payments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial contracts with customers; platform terms of service; board resolution authorising the subscription business; AML policy and independent audit report; projected cash-flow forecast; business register extract and VAT registration certificate showing IT/design services rather than payment intermediation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexpected large inbound transfers from unrelated jurisdictions or crypto-exchange-linked counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Invoicing trail, trade agreement, project files or time-sheet evidence; KYC file of remitter; explanation of economic rationale; transaction-specific board resolution; confirmation that no cryptocurrency conversion is involved; anti-money laundering incidental transaction monitoring records.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant euro wire via SWIFT MT103 to the Cyprus company's IBAN. Instruction must include the exact corporate name, VAT and registration number, and a clear purpose code as required by the correspondent bank—e.g., equity injection with purpose code ''CYP-EO'' or shareholder loan with supporting loan agreement. Funds originating from shareholder accounts are subject to proof of ownership, source-of-funds documentation, and AML verification before credit acceptance; high-value injections require sworn statement from the beneficial owner and a board resolution.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for design subscription services are generally executed via SWIFT MT103 or SEPA credit transfers with invoice reference; for higher-value procurement of licensing or software development, documentary commercial letters of credit under UCP 600 may be utilised. Domestic supplier payments are made via SEPA using IBAN and BIC; cross-border payments outside the EEA use SWIFT with appropriate narrative and compliance screening.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (plain vanilla deliverable EUR/USD or EUR/GBP) with licensed Cypriot credit institutions
FX swaps for temporary conversion of export proceeds into euro
Cross-currency basis swaps, limited to hedging actual commercial exposure, not speculative
Non-deliverable forwards, solely for documented underlying exposure against non-convertible countercurrencies, arranged via an approved international dealer under EMIR-compliant execution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRCOR), Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 June of every calendar year, irrespective of incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment of EUR 50 if settled between 1 July and 31 August; EUR 75 if settled thereafter. Unpaid levy blocks filing of the annual return and issuance of certificates of good standing; persistent non-payment triggers a Registrar warning notice and administrative strike-off under the Companies Law.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRCOR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 calendar days of the anniversary of incorporation, filed annually
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of EUR 25 per month or part of a month, capped at EUR 300 after 12 months; a company that remains in default for approximately 3 months is exposed to a Gazette strike-off notice and subsequent administrative dissolution, with directors personally liable for continuing statutory obligations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Form TD4) with Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Tax Department, Ministry of Finance (Cyprus Tax Commissioner)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of the accounting period; 31 December for a 31-December year-end company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fixed penalty of EUR 100 for a late return; EUR 50 per month of delay in submitting audited financial statements, capped at EUR 600; unpaid tax accrues statutory interest of 1.75% per annum plus an additional tax of 10% on the outstanding amount; prolonged default triggers enforced collection and director liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Central UBO Register Update after Share Transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Central Beneficial Ownership Register, Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRCOR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 calendar days of any change in ultimate beneficial ownership, including any share transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal offence punishable by a fine up to EUR 200 and/or imprisonment up to 1 year for late or incorrect central-register filings; EUR 100 fine and/or up to 6 months' imprisonment for internal-register maintenance failures; repeated breaches also expose the corporate service provider to AML-related administrative sanctions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit applies unless the company qualifies as small under two of three criteria for two consecutive years: annual turnover not exceeding EUR 70,000; balance-sheet total not exceeding EUR 350,000; average number of employees not exceeding 5. The exemption is unavailable to public-interest entities, listed companies, banks, insurers and other regulated businesses, and a shareholder holding at least 10% of the issued capital may still require an audit. A subscription-based UI/UX design agency with recurring revenue above EUR 70,000 will normally be subject to statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as issued by the IASB and adopted by the EU; Cyprus does not apply a separate local GAAP and does not permit IFRS for SMEs in statutory accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Cyprus does not require a free-standing calendar-annual UBO declaration. After every share transfer, the company must update its internal beneficial-ownership register and file the change with the DRCOR central register within 14 calendar days, reflecting the new ownership percentages and control structure. The registered agent verifies UBO continuity at each annual return (HE43) preparation and reviews the register ahead of each meeting of members; the agent's separate AML/accountable-person obligations operate as a de facto annual confirmation cycle.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 770-1,650 (EUR 700-1,500) per annum for a compliant registered office and licensed corporate agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,100-2,750 (EUR 1,000-2,500) for a low-risk digital design subscription agency with clean Stripe and Wise statements

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory 12.5% headline rate with effective reduction to approximately 2.5% on qualifying intellectual property profits under the Cyprus IP Box regime (80% deduction of qualifying IP gross revenue attributable to R&D nexus assets). Additional reliefs: participation exemption on dividends earned from qualifying overseas subsidiaries and on capital gains from the disposal of securities, notional interest deduction (NID) on new qualifying equity subscribed and paid in, 50% payroll deduction for qualifying non-resident high-skilled employees engaged in approved digital activities under the Cyprus tax relief scheme, and unconditional 5-year tax loss carryforward for tax years commencing after 1 January 2019.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cyprus Corporate Income Tax Return Form IR4 filed exclusively through the Taxisnet electronic filing portal operated by the Cyprus Tax Department (ecd.tax).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The IR4 must be submitted no later than 6 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a 31 December year-end the statutory deadline is 30 June of the following year. Provisional (temporary) tax is payable in two equal installments on 31 July and 31 December of the tax year, with the final settlement balance being due on the IR4 filing deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 – Company identification (legal name, TIN, trade name, registered office)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the Cyprus private limited company, 8-digit Tax Identification Number (TIN), exact registered office address, and the fiscal year-end under review.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Cypriot entity identification exactly as registered in the Department of Registrar of Companies; state the foreign parent's country of residence in the supplemental information only where a treaty protection claim is pending; do not register the foreign parent's address as the Cyprus place of effective management.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 – Business activity classification and commencement details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Descriptive trade activity and standardized ISIC classification code; for UI/UX subscription services, the primary code is ISIC 7410 (specialised design activities) with commercial model 'Design-as-a-Service'.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Describe the subscription model as a recurring services contract performed by Cyprus-based designers and project managers; confirm that the activity is not carried on through any other permanent establishment outside Cyprus when relying on a tax residence certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 11 – Gross revenue from taxable activities
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross subscription receipts and one-off design service fees invoiced to international clients, net of value added tax where invoiced as an EU VATABLE supply.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognise revenue on the accruals basis consistent with IFRS 15 as applied in the Cyprus statutory accounts; exclude any amounts attributable to a permanent establishment comprised in a foreign branch; retain merchant settlement reports from Stripe and Wise as year-end reconciliation evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 12 – Cost of sales and direct staff costs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct salaries of UI/UX designers, project-based subcontracted freelancers, SaaS software subscription tools, cloud hosting, and other directly attributable service delivery costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only costs legally borne by the Cyprus entity are deductible; intercompany recharges from foreign related suppliers must be supported by written agreements, service evidence, and arm's length pricing under the Cyprus Transfer Pricing Rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Office rent, utilities, professional legal and accounting fees, marketing, platform payment fees (Stripe/Wise), and insurance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible items including penalties, taxes on profits, interest on underpaid tax, and private expenditure of directors; expenses incurred by a foreign agent on behalf of the Cypriot company must be properly recharged through a valid debit note.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax depreciation claims under the Cyprus Capital Allowances regime, including computers and design hardware at 20% straight-line, software at 33.3% straight-line, and motor vehicles as applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No capital allowances may be claimed on assets financed or owned by a foreign related party unless legally transferred to the Cyprus company by the time of filing; provide asset register proof for each qualifying asset.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 23 – Special reliefs and deductions (IP Box, NID, loss relief)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of the 80% IP Box deduction on qualifying intangible income, notional interest deduction on eligible equity, and offsetting of previously unrelieved tax losses brought forward within the 5-year limit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only entities with relevant research and development staffing, specific user interface software IP ownership, and nexus asset documentation in Cyprus may apply the IP Box; the foreign shareholder must certify no direct claim over the Cypriot IP rights.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 28 – Chargeable income and corporate tax computation at 12.5%
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of final taxable income after adding back disallowed items and applying all reliefs, multiplied by 12.5% to determine the headline corporate tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where foreign withholding tax was suffered on income sourced in third states, include the grossed-up foreign income and claim the foreign tax credit in the available credit line; double relief on the same income is prohibited under the Cyprus-Cyprus DTA provisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 32 – Final tax payable and settlement after provisional payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of provisional tax installments already paid, computation of final balance due or refund, and declaration that the accompanying transfer pricing summary return has been correctly prepared.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Wire the final tax payment from a Cyprus bank account where possible; where refund is claimed, ensure all Stripe/Wise merchant records are stored for 6 years for potential audit challenge by the Cyprus Tax Department.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the IR4 triggers a mandatory fixed penalty of €100 plus a monthly penalty of €100 for each month of delay, subject to statutory maximum caps; taxpayers failing to file may additionally be subject to a best-of-judgment assessment. Late payment of provisional or final corporate tax attracts statutory interest at the applicable government rate on overdue amounts, and fixed penalty surcharges may be added where the tax is settled after the filing deadline.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — Cyprus imposes no dividend withholding tax on profits distributed by a Cyprus private limited company to either resident or non-resident shareholders, subject to a general absence of any domestic outbound dividend WHT levy.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: While no Cypriot statutory dividend WHT exists, the treaty relief protocol is invoked where a Cyprus DTA confers source-state withholding rights on the other contracting state or where a foreign tax authority requires proof of Cypriot residence. The administrative chain: (1) obtain a Cyprus Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the Cyprus Tax Department for the relevant fiscal year; (2) prepare a beneficial ownership declaration signed by the ultimate shareholder confirming no nominee or conduit arrangement; (3) submit the foreign shareholder's TRC issued by the competent authority of the residence state; (4) file the Cypriot 'Application for Treaty Relief' and a self-declaration through Taxisnet where the Cyprus entity acts as the paying agent; and (5) retain all documentation in the statutory books for audit. For dividends moving to an EU parent, the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive applies without any withholding requirement and no practical filing protocol beyond the shareholder residence certificate is necessary.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Cyprus withholding tax on outbound royalties to non-residents is 0%; outbound interest to non-residents is also 0% under the Cyprus Income Tax Law. Under most signed double tax treaties, Cyprus reserves a source-state rate on interest and royalties of between 0% and 10%, and where the recipient is an EU company the EU Interest and Royalties Directive eliminates any source taxation subject to the beneficial owner test. Payments from a Cyprus company to a low-tax or non-DTA jurisdiction remain untaxed at source but must satisfy arm's length pricing and economic substance requirements to avoid adjustment under the Cyprus GAAR.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Transfer Pricing Summary Documentation (Form TD1) filing via Taxisnet applies where the aggregate value of controlled transactions in a tax year exceeds €1,000,000. Full Local File and Master File documentation should be prepared and retained to support the arm's length character of all related-party dealings and must be produced within 60 days of a formal request by the Cyprus Tax Department.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Cyprus adopts economic substance as an administrative and judicial doctrine drawn from the Income Tax Law management-and-control test, the EU/ATAD General Anti-Abuse Rule, and the OECD BEPS nexus approach. A Cyprus company benefits from the 12.5% regime only if effective management and key decision-making occurs on the island, with own premises, locally employed qualified staff, operating board meetings in Cyprus, and substantive local control over the UI/UX design contracts, invoicing, cash management, and intellectual property ownership. Shell arrangements are rebutted by the Cyprus Tax Department through residency denial, withdrawal of tax residence certificates, and re-characterisation of income flows.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deleting or under-invoicing subscription revenue received through Stripe or Wise payment gateways; issuing invoices to foreign clients on behalf of a non-existent Cypriot service capacity; dishonestly under-reporting gross receipts in the IR4 while simultaneously claiming high deductibles for personal spending.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil: revised assessment for the evaded tax, statutory interest at government rates, and penalty surcharges of up to double the evaded tax. Criminal: conviction on indictment carries a fine and/or imprisonment of up to five years for fraudulent tax evasion; offences are prosecuted by the Republic under the Assessment and Collection of Taxes Law Cap. 4.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly submit false returns face personal criminal sanctions, travel bans, and disqualification orders; where the misdeclaration is connected to insolvency, directors may be personally liable for fraudulent trading under the Cyprus Companies Law Cap. 113, with civil restitution to the revenue and creditors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Artificial Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Cyprus LTD as a passive billing shell while all UI/UX design staff, servers, contracting, and decision-making remain in a non-resident jurisdiction; appointing nominee directors with no commercial oversight; maintaining no physical office; allowing a foreign entity to direct bank accounts and subscription payment routing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of corporate tax residence status; re-attribution of worldwide profits to the real place of effective management at the applicable foreign tax rate; refusal of the Cyprus Tax Residency Certificate for treaty purposes; retroactive application of the Cyprus GAAR with reassessments at 12.5% on undisclosed income, penalty surcharges, and cancellation of existing tax clearance certificates. The company may simultaneously lose the right to apply the IP Box relief and participation exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil liability for fraudulent misrepresentations in statutory declarations; personal clawback of distributions made without proper substance; criminal exposure of directors who knowingly facilitated artificial profit allocation and shadow-director liability for foreign persons exercising de facto control.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and TD1 Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file Form TD1 where controlled transactions exceed the €1,000,000 threshold; inflating management fees paid to a foreign group entity without an arm's length benchmarking study; charging arbitrary mark-ups or royalties to related design subscribers in zero-tax jurisdictions; invoicing below cost of service from Cyprus to a related foreign distributor.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Arm's-length recharacterisation of the intercompany pricing with additional tax, interest at the statutory rate, and penalty surcharges of up to 100% of the additional assessed tax; monthly late-filing penalties for the omitted TD1 form; active listing in the high-risk audit programme and automatic referral to the transfer pricing unit of the Cyprus Tax Department.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved the mispricing are jointly and severally liable for the penalty amounts if the company cannot pay; exit bans may be imposed to block departure until settlement; criminal proceedings apply where the transfer pricing distortion is collusive and fraudulent. Directors of the Cypriot entity may also owe indemnities to minority shareholders for preference enforcement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing subscription payments for a sanctioned person or entity through the Stripe/Wise merchant rails; accepting monies from undisclosed beneficial owners using shell-client intermediaries; deliberately failing to maintain beneficial ownership registers under the Cyprus Companies Law; accelerating fund transfers to a jurisdiction linked to terrorist financing; issuing a subscription refund to a third party unrelated to the original purchaser.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fines of up to €500,000 and imprisonment of up to ten years for money-laundering offences under the Cyprus Prevention and Suppression of Money Laundering Law 188(I)/2007; immediate freezing of merchant accounts by payment processors; compulsory filing of Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) to the Cyprus Unit for Combating Money Laundering (MOKAS); revocation of any operating licences and prohibition against holding beneficiary ownership in regulated sectors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who direct, facilitate, or knowingly ignore suspicious payment routing are personally indictable; personal assets may be confiscated under proceeds-of-crime legislation; directors face travel bans, wealth freezing orders, disqualification of up to five years, and personal criminal liability without any corporate veil protection.
